jobs.occupation: Research Associate / PhD Student /PostDoc (m/f/x) in Near-Memory Computing for RISC-V (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description:
TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. Founded in 1828, today it is a globally oriented, regionally anchored top university as it focuses on the grand challenges of the 21st century. It develops innovative solutions for the world's most pressing issues. In research and academic programs, the university unites the natural and engineering sciences with the humanities, social sciences and medicine. This wide range of disciplines is a special feature, facilitating interdisciplinarity and transfer of science to society. As a modern employer, it offers attractive working conditions to all employees in teaching, research, technology and administration. The goal is to promote and develop their individual abilities while empowering everyone to reach their full potential. TUD embodies a university culture that is characterized by cosmopolitanism, mutual appreciation, thriving innovation and active participation. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.

At the Faculty of Computer Science, Institute of Computer Engineering, the Chair of Adaptive Dynamic Systems offers a full-time position as

Research Associate / PhD Student /PostDoc (m/f/x)

in Near-Memory Computing for RISC-V 

(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)

starting as soon as poosible. The position is limited to 2 years, with the option of extension. The period of employment is governed by the Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz – WissZeitVG). The position aims at obtaining further academic qualification.

The Chair of Adaptive Dynamic Systems conducts research in the fields of reconfigurable computing, domain-specific computer architectures, networks-on-chip (NoCs), methods and algorithms for application parallelization, simulators and virtual platforms for application- and architecture exploration, hardware/software co-design and operating/runtime systems. Typical application domains are e.g. signal-/image processing and machine learning.

Tasks: 

- modeling and simulation of near-memory computing architectures for RISC-V processors using SystemC and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs)
- developing machine learning methods to identify suitable computational kernels and optimize their placement within the processor memory hierarchy
- contributing, administrating and reporting in (inter-)national research and development projects
- publishing and presenting results at international conferences
- close cooperation with academic and industrial cooperation partners

Requirements: 

- excellent university degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) in computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering or a related field
- very good programming skills in C/C++
- fluency in English; knowledge of German is an advantage
- high self-motivation, commitment, and flexibility, as well as the ability to work effectively in an international team
- strong background in one or more of the following areas: computer architecture, RISC-V, FPGA-based systems, SystemC, VHDL or Verilog, high-level synthesis, compiler frameworks, artificial intelligence, and/or machine learning

We offer an excellent working environment in an international team with many career development possibilities.

TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.

Application:

Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents including a CV, a brief proposal describing their research experience and interests and an official transcript of coursework and grades using the reference number“ADS_26-01” by October 8, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de (https://securemail.tu-dresden.de) by sending it as a single pdf file to ads@mailbox.tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:ads@mailbox.tu-dresden.de) or to:

TU Dresden, Chair of Adaptive Dynamic Systems, Prof. Dr.-Ing. Diana Göhringer, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.

Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.

TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.

Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis (https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis) .

jobs.occupation: PhD Student (m/w/d) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
Universitätsklinikum Düsseldorf (UKD) is the largest hospital in the state capital and one of the most important medical centres in North Rhine-Westphalia. The 9,300 employees of UKD and its subsidiaries ensure that more than 45,000 patients are treated as inpatients and 270,000 as outpatients every year. UKD stands for international excellence in patient care, research and teaching, and for innovative and safe diagnostics, therapy and prevention. Patients benefit from the intensive interdisciplinary cooperation of 60 clinics and institutes. The particular strength of the university hospital lies in the close interlinking of clinical care and research for the safe application of new methods. At UKD, the medicine of tomorrow is created. Every day.

The Institute of Pathology at Universitätsklinikum Düsseldorf (Director: Univ.-Prof. Dr. Irene Esposito), in a joint project with the Institute of Pharmaceutical Biology and Biotechnology (Prof. Dr. Nicole Teusch), is offering, at the earliest possible date, a
PhD position (m/f/d)

in the field of 3D Tumour Biology for Personalized Drug Discovery.

Part-time, 65% of the weekly working hours.

The appointment is initially limited to a period of 2 years, with the option of extension. This is a qualification position within the meaning of the German Act on Fixed-Term Employment Contracts in Academia (WissZeitVG, § 2 para. 1).

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest cancers, largely because its dense stromal and immune microenvironment drives therapy resistance that conventional cell-line models and 3D organoids fail to capture. In this joint project, we are looking for a PhD candidate to characterise an ex vivo PDAC tissue model that preserves native tissue architecture together with the stromal and immune compartments, and to develop it into a working platform for drug testing and screening. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by both groups and fully embedded in each - a rare opportunity to combine pathology, tumour biology and pharmacology within one project.
Establishment and characterisation of ex vivo PDAC tissue cultures (murine and human)
Histopathology and digital image analysis (QuPath)
Generation of transcriptomic data and independent downstream bioinformatic analysis
Analysis of (cell-type-specific) drug responses
Validation of the findings in patient-derived tumour tissue

Master's degree in biology, biomedicine, biochemistry, or a related life-science discipline
Research experience in cell and/or tissue culture and in standard molecular biology methods
Interest in transcriptomic data and the willingness to grow into its bioinformatic analysis

A plus, not a must: prior experience with histology, primary tissue culture or RNA-seq analysis, or work with animal-derived material (FELASA certification an advantage)
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work efficiently both independently and in a team
Excellent English communication skills (written and spoken)

A fully funded, three-year position at the interface of pathology, tumour biology and pharmacology
25.025 weekly working hours
Access to the infrastructure and expertise of two established institutes
State-of-the-art facilities and current methods
International, engaged teams with structured doctoral supervision, including regular project meetings
Support for conference attendance and method training
Structured graduate programmes, e.g. through the Düsseldorf School of Oncology (DSO)
All benefits customary in the public sector, e.g. a company supplementary pension
Affordable catering options
Staff accommodation
Day-care facilities for children

jobs.description:
The Department of Pediatric Oncology, Hematology and Clinical Immunology at the University Hospital Düsseldorf (UKD) at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU), headed by Prof. Dr. Arndt Borkhardt, is one of the leading clinical centers for the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer in Germany. The clinic is part of the University Tumor Center (UTZ) at the UKD and the Center for Integrative Oncology Aachen-Bonn-Cologne-Düsseldorf (CIO-ABCD), which is funded by the German Cancer Aid. It is a founding partner of the German Consortium for Translational Cancer Research (DKTK) Essen-Düsseldorf and participates in international research consortia and study groups. The clinic operates a fully equipped research laboratory (safety level 1 and 2 according to the Genetic Engineering/Biotechnology Ordinance, including a GMP, next generation sequencing, flow cytometry, life cell imaging, and high-throughput drug testing facility) with 5 research groups and >30 staff working in an interdisciplinary manner on the fundamentals of childhood cancer and in the field of therapy optimization. We are seeking a highly motivated and creative PhD Student to join our research program in the field of amino acid homeostasis and cancer metabolism, with an anticipated start date of 02/2027. The successful candidate will work on the ERC-funded project “POWERFUL” (Deciphering how cancer cells fuel themselves to advance personalized treatment strategies).
The PhD student will take a leading role in understanding how cancer cells sense and respond to amino acid availability, and how to translate this knowledge into precision-based treatment strategies. This position requires scientific independence and the opportunity to contribute intellectually to experimental design, data interpretation, and publication strategy. The candidate will employ and further develop advanced experimental models and methodologies, including organoid systems, patient-derived xenografts (PDXs), CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing, multiparameter flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, FRET assays, protein interaction and signaling assays, as well as in vitro and in vivo drug screening approaches.
Candidates should have a very good understanding of and experience with standard molecular biology techniques including but not limited to tissue culture, genome editing, FACS analysis, confocal microscopy, immunoblot, and PCR/qPCR. Experience with animal models is a plus (as is FELASA B certification). Willingness to learn and work with murine experimental models is a fundamental requirement. - Master in natural sciences or related field

- Solid experience with cancer models (e.g. organoids, PDXs) and drug-response studies
- expertise in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including mammalian tissue culture, genome editing, FACS/flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, immunoblotting, and PCR/qPCR.
- Excellent capability to develop new aspects and projects within the given research focus
- Excellent written and spoken English language skills, German language skills are a plus
- Organizational and project management experience
- Willingness to cooperate and ability to work in a team
- Experience in working with animals (FELASA B) is a plus, willingness to work with animals a requisite Remuneration is based on TV-L in pay grade 13 (65%), taking into account all previous periods of employment. The employment contract will be concluded with Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf.

jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
OUR COMPANY

At Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. As a family owned company, we focus on long-term performance. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture.
The Position
Lead the Future of Medicine - as (Senior) Clinical Program Lead in the Therapeutic Area of Pulmonology.
To ensure the fastest and most focused path from strategy to patients, we are evolving our OneHP organization. Together, we are simplifying our structures, strengthening the accountability of Therapeutic Areas, and creating clear interfaces between Innovation and Business. This ensures that our assets are efficiently transformed into successful brands, with the ultimate goal of delivering lasting value to patients around the world.
We are looking for a highly motivated physician-scientist to support the late-stage development of innovative therapies in bronchiectasis. As (Senior) Clinical Program Lead, you will play a key role in advancing a Phase III program through submission activities, pediatric development strategy, and cross-functional clinical leadership.
This position can be filled in Ingelheim or Biberach.

In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/x) in Machine Learning for Light-Induced Excited-State Dynamics in Materials

The successful applicant will join the research group of Prof. Silvana Botti at the Research Center Future Energy Materials and Systems (RC FEMS) and the Ruhr University Bochum (RUB). The group develops first-principles and machine-learning methods to describe electronic excitations, light–matter interaction, and ultrafast dynamics in materials and at functional interfaces. The newly founded Research Center focuses on developing innovative materials and systems for sustainable energy applications. The center’s research areas include photovoltaics, thermoelectricity, energy storage, fuel cells, and sustainable chemical processes, among others. Its interdisciplinary approach involves collaborations between physicists, chemists, engineers, and material scientists to address the challenges of transitioning to a low-carbon economy. The center also offers opportunities for graduate students and postdoctoral researchers to participate in cutting-edge research projects and receive advanced training in the field of energy materials and systems. The chair of Prof. Botti is affiliated with the Faculty of Physics and Astronomy of the Ruhr University Bochum. This faculty is a leading research and teaching institution in the fields of experimental and theoretical physics and astronomy, with a focus on condensed matter physics, astrophysics, and particle physics.

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher (m/f/x) with a strong background in condensed matter physics and a proven record in developing machine-learning methods. The position focuses on the development of new computational approaches that combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory (rt-TDDFT), nonadiabatic excited-state dynamics, and machine learning, in order to reach the time and length scales needed to describe light-induced phenomena in complex materials.

Scope: full-time

- investigate ultrafast light-induced processes in materials, such as photoinduced structural phase transitions, coupled electron–phonon dynamics, and non-equilibrium carrier and lattice dynamics, including materials and interfaces relevant for energy applications

jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (26.2878 hours/week = 66%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

PhD position (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholds

The work of the chair of experimental physics 1 focuses on basic research: One of the most essential elements of todays education and research is to gain a better understanding of the structure of matter and the fundamental principles of nature. In this process the basic research of physics plays an important role as it provides a base for technical innovations and development. Hadron Physics deals with strong interacting particles consisting of quarks and gluons. Among those hadrons also rank the building blocks of the atomic nucleus, the proton and the neutron. There are many other hadrons that can only be created via collisions of high energetic particles in big particle accelerators. The created hadrons are detected by modern and complex detectors to examine their composition and interactions.

The position is embedded in two research programs. DEMOS ("Democratizing Models") is an ErUM research initiative developing a federated, interoperable standard for describing, sharing and re-evaluating physics models across particle, hadron, nuclear, neutrino and astroparticle physics. Hadronic coupled-channel amplitudes are one of its flagship applications: they are analytically intricate and rarely reproducible from the publication alone, which makes them an ideal test case for the new standard. HADRON 2030 is an intercollaborative research network dedicated to studies of hadron physics. Within the ExHAT (Exploration of Heavy Hadrons at Thresholds) project, we will explore heavy hadrons at thresholds using spectroscopy methods with LHCb data and inclusive production studies with ALICE. The flagship case is the doubly charmed tetraquark Tcc(3875)+, which lies a fraction of an MeV below the D0 D*+ threshold. Line shape, pole position, three-body DD-pi dynamics and isospin breaking have to be disentangled in a joint effort of theory and experiment.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 years
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-10-06

Your tasks:

- Application of advanced methods of data selection, efficiency and resolution
studies within LHCb data analysis.
- Construction, fitting and analytic continuation of coupled-channel scattering
amplitudes.
- Decipherment and serialization of the complex amplitudes in the DEMOS /
amplitude-serialization format.
- Collaboration within the DEMOS / HADRON 2030 networks.
Exchange with the experimental collaborations
[LHCb, BESIII, Belle II, GlueX, ...] and with EFT/lattice QCD groups.

Your profile:

- Master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, completed by the starting date.
- Background in experimental particle physics or hadron physics, and familiarity

with quantum field theory and scattering theory.

- Good scientific programming skills (Julia, Python or C++) and experience with

version control and reproducible workflows.

- Very good command of written and spoken English.
- Interest in working at the interface between theory and experiment and in open,

reusable research software.

jobs.description:
The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.

The following full-time (38.5 hours/week) position is to be filled as soon as possible at the Center of Neurology of the University Hospital Bonn:

Postdoctoral Researcher in Computer Vision and Multimodal AI for the Early Detection of Parkinson’s Disease (m/w/d)

The position is fixed-term until 30 September 2028 due to the duration of the research project.

Parkinson’s disease is usually diagnosed only after substantial neurodegeneration has already occurred. Subtle changes in movement, facial expression and speech may emerge years earlier, but current clinical assessments are not designed to detect and quantify them at scale. We believe that computer vision and multimodal AI can help close this gap - and that meaningful progress requires researchers who want to apply cutting-edge methods to a major clinical challenge.

Our goal is to develop objective and scalable digital tools for the early detection and monitoring of Parkinson’s disease. We combine video-based analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and limb movements with speech, touchscreen and wearable sensor data. A particular focus is on individuals with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, who are at high risk of developing Parkinson’s disease or related neurodegenerative disorders.

The group of Prof. Dr. Michael Sommerauer at the Center of Neurology at the University Hospital Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join our interdisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will take a leading role in the development of the computer vision components of bradyMX, our multimodal digital motor assessment platform. The position is embedded in the ERC-funded Re-START PD research program and offers the opportunity to work with unique, deeply phenotyped clinical cohorts and longitudinal datasets. Rather than developing methods in isolation, you will work closely with clinicians and neuroscientists to translate methodological advances into tools that may improve patient stratification, clinical trials and, ultimately, the way Parkinson’s disease is detected.

Please submit your application as a single PDF, including: 

• a cover letter describing your scientific interests and motivation for joining the group 

• a curriculum vitae including a publication list 

• contact details for at least two referees

Your responsibilities:

- Lead the development of computer vision methods for quantifying subtle motor abnormalities from clinical video recordings
- Develop robust pipelines for human pose estimation, facial and body landmark detection, movement segmentation, tracking, feature extraction and automated quality control
- Design and evaluate machine-learning and deep-learning models for the analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and upper- and lower-limb movements
- Investigate temporal modelling, representation learning and interpretable movement features for the detection and monitoring of early motor dysfunction
- Integrate video-derived features with complementary digital modalities such as speech, touchscreen tasks, inertial sensors and clinical assessments
- Evaluate model robustness and generalizability across participants, recording conditions, devices and international study sites
- Work closely with the clinical research team on study design, data collection, annotation strategies and the interpretation of model outputs
- Prepare scientific manuscripts, present results at international conferences and contribute to grant applications
- Support the supervision of doctoral, Master’s and medical students

Your profile:

- - A doctoral degree in computer vision, machine learning, computer science, biomedical engineering, medical informatics or a closely related discipline
- Strong experience in machine learning and deep learning for image, video or human movement analysis
- Excellent programming skills in Python and practical experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX
- Experience in one or more of the following areas: human pose estimation, motion tracking, action recognition, temporal modelling, self-supervised learning, multimodal learning or domain adaptation
- A sound understanding of experimental design, quantitative model evaluation and reproducible research practices
- Experience with version control and collaborative software development; knowledge of containerized workflows and high-performance computing is an advantage
- Interest in translating methodological advances into clinically meaningful applications; previous experience in Parkinson’s disease or medical research is welcome but not required
- A high degree of scientific curiosity, independence and commitment to rigorous research
- Strong communication skills and enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international environment
- Very good command of written and spoken English; German language skills are not required

What we offer:

- Access to unique, deeply phenotyped cohorts of individuals at risk of Parkinson’s disease, healthy controls and patients with early Parkinson’s disease
- Rich video, sensor and clinical datasets collected using standardized multimodal assessment protocols
- A direct path from methodological development to external validation and clinically relevant application

- An excellent research environment at the University Hospital Bonn, the University of Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases

jobs.description:
About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) is a
joint venture between four technology leaders, TSMC, Bosch, Infineon
and NXP, to establish a state-of-the-art semiconductor fab in the
heart of Europe. ESMC represents our shared commitment to
strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. Für unsere
zukünftige Fab in Dresden suchen wir eine/n hochmotivierte/n und
engagierte/n: Equipment Engineer (m/f/d) – Start Date: 1 October
2026 At ESMC, the Equipment Engineer supports the installation,
maintenance, troubleshooting, and optimization of advanced
semiconductor manufacturing equipment in a cleanroom environment. As
part of a high-volume 24/7 fab operation, the role focuses on ensuring
tool performance, improving uptime, reducing defects, and supporting
stable production. The position requires openness to scheduled and
occasional shift work, on call duty, includes an initial induction and
training period in Dresden of one month, followed by one year of
on-the-job training in Taiwan. If you are interested in advancing your
career in semiconductor manufacturing, learning from one of the
world’s leading semiconductor companies, and joining an
international and diverse team on a unique learning journey, apply now
with your English CV. Tasks 1. Maintain equipment performance in a
cleanroom environment to support stable, high-quality production. 2.
Handle on-duty tasks and perform fundamental alarm troubleshooting. 3.
Install and qualify new tool sets according to project plans and
schedules. 4. Identify root causes and solve critical equipment
issues. 5. Improve tool uptime and availability while driving defect
reduction. 6. Identify and pursue opportunities for hardware
capability enhancement. 7. Build defense and monitoring systems to
prevent equipment failures and performance loss. 8. Manage vendor
relationships and act as module liaison with facilities, vendors, and
manufacturing shift personnel. 9. Support scheduled night shifts,
evening shifts, weekend work, on-duty assignments, and on-call duties
as required in a 24/7 high-volume manufacturing environment. Profile

1. Legally eligible to work in Germany. 2. Available for approximately
one year of on-the-job training in Taiwan. 3. Open for scheduled and
occasional shift work, on call duty. 4. Degree in electronics,
electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, mechanics,
mechatronics, material engineering, or an equivalent field. 5.
Practical experience in a mechanical or equipment-related field. 6.
Understanding of technical documentation and schematics. 7. Knowledge
of semiconductor manufacturing is a plus. 8. Fluent in English with
good command of German. 9. Hands-on working attitude with an open
mindset. 10. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. 11. Able
to perform physical work on tools in a cleanroom environment.

commence on October 1, 2026, in Dresden. Depending on your needs and
timeline preferences, January 1, 2027, can be considered as an
alternative start date. Onboarding and International Training: The
first month of your employment will be spent in Dresden. Following
this initial onboarding, training, and integration with your new team
members, you will travel to Taiwan for a one-year on-the-job training
and knowledge transfer program. Your training in Taiwan will involve
close collaboration with experienced TSMC engineering teams. You may
also receive additional training and support at TSMC’s
state-of-the-art Newcomer Training Center in Taichung. Training
Logistics: For employees requiring accommodation during the first
month in Dresden, and who reside more than 90 minutes away, ESMC will
organize appropriate temporary lodging. This provision does not apply
to employees who establish a residential address in Dresden (e.g., to
expedite work permit procedures away from their original place of
residence) or who terminate a personal lease contract in Dresden prior
to their planned departure to Taiwan. Furthermore, ESMC will organize
and provide air and ground transportation from Dresden to Taichung
(Taiwan) and back at the conclusion of the training. Accommodation in
Taiwan will be provided in one of TSMC’s modern and comfortable
company dormitories. Role Requirements and Expectations: This is a
unique opportunity to gain exposure to TSMC’s world-leading advanced
manufacturing practices and actively contribute to building ESMC from
the ground up. As a start-up organization, ESMC offers the opportunity
to play an active role in shaping the company’s culture, future
organization and ways of working. Candidates should be comfortable in
a dynamic environment where certain operational details such as

during the ramp-up phase. This role is ideal for individuals with a
